faq.a: Zubair is associated with the Arabic form زُبَيْر, whose core sense is zubair; strong, firm.

faq.q: What is the origin of Zubair?
faq.a: Zubair is associated with Arabic. Zubair is Arabic زُبَيْر (Zubayr), a diminutive associated with the sense 'strong, firm'. It was borne by a companion of the Prophet.
Yes — the underlying form زُبَيْر is Arabic.
Zubair can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zubair should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zubayr is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zubair mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zubair is rendered زبیر and carries the sense زبیر، مضبوط.

faq.q: What does Zubair mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zubair is rendered زبیر and carries the sense زبیر، نیرومند.
A romanized syllable approximation is zu-bair. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zubair?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zubair, zubair. Script forms are زبير, زبیر, زُبَيْر, ज़ुबैर.

faq.q: Is Zubair a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
